name: UI and UX product design
one_line: A software-product interface design lifecycle in which research and requirements become flows and wireframes, an interactive prototype is tested with users, findings drive revisions, and an approved design is handed to implementation; interface topic or a design-tool file alone is insufficient.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are recognition signals, not extraction licences. The creative schema declares no field rows, so this template writes no creative facts and no folder dimensions.

a research-to-design packet that joins a research plan or interview synthesis to named user needs, journeys, task flows, or acceptance criteria and then to a wireframe or screen inventory; a research PDF without a design artifact is not enough

a wireframe structure with repeated screen or state identifiers, navigation paths, annotations, and interaction notes, paired with an interactive prototype or linked screen set whose links resolve to those states

a usability-test structure that identifies a participant or test session, task script, observed result or issue, and a reference to the exact screen, flow, or prototype state; a generic survey or product analytics export does not qualify alone

a revision chain in which findings or review comments cite a screen/flow version and a later prototype, annotated wireframe, or decision log records the response; FINAL or v2 tokens alone are not approval

a product-design handoff structure containing approved screen or component references, interaction/state specifications, accessibility notes, and an implementation-facing handoff or acceptance record; a static mockup without product context remains ordinary creative work

a design-system library structure with named components, variants, states, usage guidance, and links to product screens, where the library governs an interface rather than being a downloaded UI kit or isolated visual asset

a product backlog or decision record that explicitly links a user problem or requirement to a flow, prototype, test result, and disposition; generic project status without interface evidence belongs to project delivery
needs_llm: deciding whether a research document is discovery for an interface, market research, academic research, or a general product strategy record when the title is broad
matching an unlabelled screenshot, board, or prototype link to a product and lifecycle stage when the file contains only screen copy and no project identifier
deciding whether a Figma, Sketch, XD, Framer, or presentation artifact is a working prototype, a static presentation, a portfolio case study, a downloaded template, or a handoff copy
distinguishing usability evidence from stakeholder preference: a participant task, observed outcome, and cited interface state are stronger than a comment saying that a screen feels confusing
deciding whether a component library is the product team's governed design system or a stock asset library, based on variants, usage rules, ownership, and links to product screens
separating a product requirement from a general software ticket when the ticket mentions a page or button but has no user problem, flow, screen reference, or acceptance evidence

deciding whether an approved screen is approved for research, visual direction, engineering implementation, or release; the lifecycle event must remain unknown when the approver and artifact are not identified
never_alone: a design_creative source type or .fig, .sketch, .xd, .framer, .proto, .pdf, .png, or .pptx extension alone
the words UX, UI, product, screen, wireframe, prototype, usability, user journey, design system, component, approved, or handoff alone
a product, company, app, brand, or team name without a role-bearing interface lifecycle and an identified design artifact
a screenshot or screen-shaped image without positive evidence of a software interface, product context, or design-work relationship; missing EXIF is not proof of a screenshot
a Figma/Sketch/Adobe XD file with frames or artboards but no evidence that it is an authored product-design work rather than a template, presentation, or portfolio case study
a component name, colour token, typography specimen, or icon set alone; these may be stock assets, brand identity material, or implementation code
a usability survey, analytics dashboard, support ticket, or interview transcript alone; research becomes this template's evidence only when tied to interface tasks or states
a Jira, Linear, Trello, or project-status export alone; implementation planning and governance are not product design without linked flows, prototypes, tests, or handoff material
a FINAL, v1, v2, approved, release, or sign-off filename token alone
a bounded download session, shared folder, prototype URL, or same-day cluster of files alone; transport and co-occurrence do not establish topic or lifecycle
author metadata, a designer's name, or a parent folder named Product, UX, Design, or Research as a destination-bearing fact

grouping_reasons: one product problem or feature from discovery through approved interface handoff
one research study and the flows, prototypes, findings, and decisions it informs
one screen or flow across wireframe, prototype, test, revision, and approval versions
one product release or feature increment's design decisions and implementation handoff
one governed component or design-system library and the product screens that consume it
one usability session or test round tied to exact prototype states
one accepted design package across design-tool sources, exports, specifications, and handoff notes

template.why: The creative schema is a launch placeholder with no declared fields, so this template may not serialize project, stage, artifact_type, or client as dimensions. If R1c adopts the schema's existing proposals, the recommended conceptual order is project or product → stage → artifact_type, with screen/flow and test-round values nested as runtime values; time is not first because research, design, testing, approval, and implementation dates are different clocks.

a feature or product name is repeated across the synthesis and a linked flow
must_not_conclude: a validated user segment
a product requirement merely from a research theme
a folder path

observations: named frames show cart, address, payment, error, and confirmation states
connectors and annotations describe task transitions and unresolved questions
must_not_conclude: that every frame is implemented
that v03 is approved
a product name from a frame label alone

observations: each page is labelled with a screen/state identifier
callouts specify empty, loading, error, and success behavior
must_not_conclude: interactive behavior from a static PDF
usability approval from a review date
that the depicted product is the corpus owner's software

observations: annotations cite prototype screen IDs and task failures

must_not_conclude: participant identity beyond what is labelled
severity or resolution unless explicitly recorded
approval of the final product

observations: tasks ask a participant to complete checkout actions
success criteria reference named prototype states and expected observations
must_not_conclude: that the test occurred
that a participant completed a task
that the script is product evidence without a linked design artifact

the sheet points back to a prototype or test session
must_not_conclude: a causal product metric from a qualitative row
a user identity from a participant code
that a disposition was implemented

that every consuming screen uses the current variant
a design-system field or folder dimension

that an adjacent repository contains the corresponding build

observations: manifest mixes design source, exported screens, tokens, handoff PDF, and a README
member names include screen/state references but archive purpose is not itself proof

that source files were delivered rather than bundled for backup

OCR may expose button labels and a product name

source files and test records are not present

observations: source tree and component imports show implementation code

collides_with.signal: The same checkout screen names, component names, and tokens can occur in a repository. A Figma handoff belongs here when design states, research/test evidence, and approval are present; source-tree/build/dependency evidence belongs to code, and neither side copies the other's facts.

The same polished screen exports or case-study PDF can be either a working product-design record or a portfolio sample. Design files and research/test lineage belong here; a retrospective presentation whose purpose is demonstrating the maker's skill belongs to career.

A screen-shaped PNG can be a captured product screen or an authored design export. Positive capture evidence and chronology support photos; linked flows, prototype states, review/test findings, or handoff evidence support this template.

falls_through_to.why: Durable design exports, specs, or handoff documents lacking reliable product-lifecycle evidence remain standalone records.
Ambiguous prototypes, feedback, and screen images whose origin or lifecycle cannot be resolved need human review.
Sparse screen captures without positive authored-design evidence are safely treated as screenshots.
General UX articles, research reports, and reusable test templates are reference material rather than product work.
Opaque proprietary design archives without a readable manifest or preview cannot safely establish the lifecycle.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased product concepts, user research notes, participant references, accessibility findings, internal strategy, credentials in prototypes, and implementation handoff details may be sensitive. This is a local-first recognition posture, not a handling class or a conclusion that every interface file is restricted.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: whether the eventual creative schema should adopt the existing canonical project, stage, artifact_type, and client proposals for product-design templates. Option A (recommended): adopt the shared keys and keep screen, flow, component, test-round, and approval labels as values or retrieval facets. Option B: defer all creative fields and retain recognition-only placeholder rows through placement. No option licenses a product_name, screen_id, user_segment, usability_score, or approval_status field in this row.
